Yarrow Underbank.narrative: I work only fallen wood. A living tree is not mine to cut, and I will not pretend otherwise, not for the giants and not for the hollow. Eirik is a good neighbour when he comes down, but the beams I have stacked and saved are the hollow's, and I will not give them up because he asks. My father taught me the woodpile before I could read, and I have built every bench and gate in this hollow from what the forest let fall.
values: the old forest's fallen wood belongs to the hollow first
good work lasts longer than the man who made it
neighbours help neighbours, but not by giving away what they need
goals: keep the saved beams for the hollow's own building
finish the new garden gates before the frost
teach Fennel the difference between fallen and living wood
master a tight joint that needs no peg, the way my father's father made them
build a proper drying rack so the beams season true before winter

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She taught me the seed rows and the old ways; I listen to her, even when we disagree.

relations.name: Marjoram Underbank
relations.label: wife
relations.note: She keeps the oven and the herb garden, and she keeps me steady when I get stubborn.

relations.name: Fennel Underbank
relations.label: son
relations.note: He follows me about the woodpile and asks more questions than I have answers for.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: She keeps the hollow's memory. I respect her, though I will speak my mind when the Old Green is at stake.

relations.name: Alder Rush
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He wants the hollow to trade more with the giants; I say we should keep what we have first.

relations.name: Osier Willow
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: He keeps the weirs and knows the streams; we agree the fallen wood should stay for the hollow.

relations.name: Eirik
relations.label: giant friend
relations.note: He is a good neighbour when he comes down, but he asks for too much this time.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: friend
relations.note: She feeds the hollow and keeps the common table; Marjoram is close with her.

relations.name: Bracken Sedge
relations.label: fellow carpenter
relations.note: We trade tools and share the fallen wood; he understands why we do not fell.

memories.gist: My father showed me how to read the grain of a fallen oak and how to tell it from a living tree.
I built the common table's benches from a single fallen ash; they are still solid after ten years.
When Eirik first came down the path, I shared my water with him and we spoke of stone and wood.
Fennel was born in the room above the workshop; I cut the cord with a blade I had made myself.
The winter the wolves came close, I stacked the fallen wood high against the fence to keep them out.

stances.why: The old forest gives us what falls; it is ours to use before anyone else's.
My father taught me, and the Old Green teaches it too.
They build in stone; they do not need our beams for their roofs.
A well-made gate or bench outlasts any argument.

pastimes: sorting and stacking the woodpile by grain and season
whittling small figures from offcuts at the bench
walking the old forest paths to see what the wind has brought down
Yarrow Underbank.calling: I make what the hollow needs from what the forest lets fall — benches, gates, beams, all of it.

Marjoram Underbank.narrative: I bake the hollow's bread and keep the herb garden by the oven. The common table is my charge, and I feed whoever comes to it, whether they come for the bread or for the talk. Yarrow is stubborn about the wood, but he is a good man, and Fennel is growing up strong. I worry about the winter store, but we have always managed.
values: a good loaf is a kind of welcome
keep the herb garden and the oven in order
goals: keep the common table supplied through the winter
dry enough herbs for the salves and the cooking
see Fennel learn a trade he loves
learn to bake a loaf that keeps a full week without going hard
dry and store enough herbs that no one in the hollow goes without a salve this winter

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: husband
relations.note: He is stubborn as a root, but he is mine, and he builds well.

relations.name: Fennel Underbank
relations.label: son
relations.note: He helps in the garden and follows his father; I want him to know both soil and wood.

relations.name: Mallow Bramblecap
relations.label: close friend
relations.note: We share the common table and the ovens; she is the sister I would have chosen.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: mother-in-law
relations.note: She keeps the seed store and knows which rows will fail; I listen to her.

relations.name: Pipwort Bramblecap
relations.label: Eldest
relations.note: She keeps the hollow's memory and its calendar; I follow her lead.

relations.name: Tansy Sedge
relations.label: friend
relations.note: We trade bread and broth and talk of the common table.

relations.name: Nesta Ashdown
relations.label: trade friend
relations.note: She trades bread with the Ferncross; we share recipes when we meet.

relations.name: Betony Mossfoot
relations.label: neighbour
relations.note: She tends the sick and makes salves; I keep her in bread when she is busy.

memories.gist: My mother taught me to bake bread in the common oven when I was tall enough to reach the peel.
The day I married Yarrow, we laid the table for the whole hollow and Mallow brought honey cakes.
Fennel was born in the room above the workshop, and Mallow was there to help.
The Lean Year did not touch the hollow's gardens much, but I still remember the hunger in the eyes of the Ferncross folk who came for bread.
I once burned a whole batch of loaves because I was arguing with Yarrow about the woodpile; we ate them anyway and laughed.

stances.why: The common table is the heart of the hollow, and no one should go hungry.
I have seen lean years; we must dry and store enough to see us through.
Yarrow and the giants can argue, but at my table we eat together.
The herb garden by the oven keeps us well through the coughs of winter.

pastimes: tending the herb garden by the oven at first light
trading gossip and news at the common table over a loaf
singing the old bread songs while the oven heats
Marjoram Underbank.calling: I bake the hollow's bread and keep the common table — feeding people is the work I was made for.

Fennel Underbank.narrative: I help in the garden and follow my father about the woodpile. I want to learn the pedlar's road from Thistle Mossfoot and see the places he talks about. The fallen wood is ours, my father says, and I believe him.
values: one day walk the pedlar's road
goals: learn the names of the herbs from mother
ask Thistle Mossfoot about the road
learn the name and use of every herb in mother's garden
be allowed to stack the small wood by himself without being told twice

relations.name: Yarrow Underbank
relations.label: father
relations.note: He lets me hold the tools and tells me about the wood.

relations.name: Marjoram Underbank
relations.label: mother
relations.note: She lets me help in the garden and gives me the first warm bread.

relations.name: Tansy Mossfoot
relations.label: playmate
relations.note: We run the garden paths and know every flower.

relations.name: Thistle Mossfoot
relations.label: pedlar friend
relations.note: He tells me about the road and the places he has seen.

relations.name: Sorrel Underbank
relations.label: grandmother
relations.note: She shows me the seed rows and tells me stories of the old forest.

memories.gist: Father let me hold the saw for the first time when we were cutting a fallen branch.
Mother showed me how to plant a seed and cover it just so.
Thistle Mossfoot came to the hollow with his packs and told me about the sea at Lanternquay.

stances.why: Father says so, and he knows about wood.
Thistle says the road is long and full of stories.

pastimes: following his father around the woodpile and handing up offcuts
playing hide-and-seek in the garden rows with Tansy Mossfoot
listening to Thistle Mossfoot's road stories with his chin in his hands
Fennel Underbank.calling: I want to walk the pedlar's road and carry things between places, like Thistle does.
